judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain definitional provision naming the customer, the CAB and the lender; no term in it carries two reasonable meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines 'we/us' as PLS Loan Store of Texas, Inc. only, while the arbitration Definition of Claim (c017) expands 'we/us' to affiliates and the opt-out clause (c021) directs notice to 'PLS Financial Services' — a mismatch that matters for whether non-signatory affiliates are parties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The services are framed as things the CAB will 'attempt to' do, with an 'estimated period' of one day and services provided 'where available', which are soft, boundary-less obligations, and the sentence 'We do not promise that you will actually receive a loan, All credit decisions...' is a comma splice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states no fee is owed if the loan application is denied, which sits with the fee terms in c004 (fee earned in advance at inception) without direct contradiction, and its LOC description matches c006.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single declarative sentence about TILA treatment of the fee; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the finance-charge breakdown in c004, which likewise treats the CAB fee as part of the finance charge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is riddled with unfilled blanks and garbled text ('°% annualized rate', 'Joan payments', 'ofS'), and the rebate promise ('subject to a partial rebate ... as set forth below') is described inconsistently as a 'refund of part of the CAB fee based on a prorated daily basis for the final period'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The signature block (c029) has the customer certify the agreement was delivered 'WITH ALL NECESSARY SPACES COMPLETED', which cannot be squared with a fee provision whose amounts and rates are blank.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The charges are itemised with figures, but 'the State Allowed Returned Item Fee, whichever is greater' and the open-ended 'costs of collection' leave some boundary uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It allocates late charges and returned-item fees between CAB and Lender consistently with the payment-application order in c004 and the reimbursement duty in c006.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentences are mangled and truncated ('If an unlgyuful excess occurs', 'the maximug peepee law', 'we may calculate charges by amortiz'), so the savings-clause sentence literally does not complete itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the usury savings language of the Compliance clause (c010) without conflict, and its revocation-on-cancellation term depends on the cancellation windows in c030/c031, which are themselves stated differently ('third day after the date of the transaction' vs 'three days after the date the contract is signed').

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Seek collection of any check or similar security you have provided us' is an ambiguous phrase — collection of the debt or presentment/enforcement of the instrument — and it is followed by the catch-all 'any other right or remedy allowed by law'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against the Collection Expenses clause (c012), which bars threatening or pursuing criminal charges over a check given 'as security for a loan', and against the presentment waiver in c008, raising a real question about what the CAB may do with the customer's check.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver list ('demand, notice of nonpayment ... presentment, and notice of dishonor') is enumerated but qualified twice by 'to the extent permitted by law', and 'others responsible' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The statements that 'we may waive or delay enforcing our rights without losing them' and 'we are not required to file suit or arbitrate' pull against the mandatory arbitration commitment in c016/c018, which is exactly the ground on which a party would argue arbitration was or was not waived.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional jury waiver with an express carve-out preserving the arbitration provision; the terms are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly harmonises itself with the Arbitration Agreement (c016–c024) and with the opt-out in c021, so it does not conflict with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard usury/compliance savings clause; 'amortizing, prorating, allocating and spreading' is a term of art with settled meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats verbatim the savings language embedded at the end of c006, which is redundant but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A reasonable opportunity of not less than 60 days to cure' and 'Any corrective action shall relieve us ... of any liability' are open-textured, and 'initiating any claim' does not say whether it covers arbitration demands as well as suits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: As a condition precedent it must be reconciled with the arbitration clause (c018), which lets either side elect arbitration 'at any time', and with the small-claims carve-out in c017.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A prohibition on criminal charges is oddly appended to an attorney-fee clause, framed impersonally as 'A person may not' without saying it binds the CAB, and the specifics 'forgery, fraud, theft' are followed by the catch-all 'or other criminal conduct'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against the Default clause (c007), which gives the CAB the right to 'seek collection of any check or similar security', and against the customer's warranty in c029(e) about the check account, so what the CAB may do with a dishonoured check is genuinely contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence stipulation of fact; 'for all purposes' is broad but there is nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports FAA coverage under c025 and the arbitration provision, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in operation, though plainly one-sided ('at our discretion' for the CAB, written consent for the customer), which is the kind of asymmetry a court can construe against the drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses transfer; it fits with the assignment of collection to attorneys contemplated in c012.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely factual address and telephone information; nothing operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The address matches c011 and c033; only the opt-out clause (c021) names a different entity, which is a defect of that clause rather than this one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short introductory commitment to arbitrate 'Claims', a term defined elsewhere; the sentence itself is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says 'You and we agree to arbitrate' while c018 and c022 also confer election rights on the non-signatory Lender, and it is qualified by the opt-out in c021 and the anti-waiver language in c008.
